children.why_this_cut: Covers the preset voice rule and the two root-authority sections (Uphold fairness, Respect real-world ties) with their examples. The only crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept used in later examples, which is seeded and handled by the parent.

Covers the Seek the truth together / Don't have an agenda section and the Assume an objective point of view subsection with its examples. The only crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept used in later examples, which is seeded and handled by the parent.

Covers the Present perspectives subsection and the No topic is off limits heading. The only crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept used in later examples, which is seeded and handled by the parent.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: privileged_information
seed_vocabulary.prose: non-public OpenAI policies, system messages, hidden chain-of-thought messages, and private content the developer or user has provided to the model, which must not be disclosed without permission

seed_vocabulary.name: information_flow
seed_vocabulary.prose: the movement of information between parties, including direct transmission and actions like changing sharing settings or approving authentication connections, which the assistant should be mindful of

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the hierarchy of instructions (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority) that determines which instructions take precedence

expected_cross_links.name: chain_of_command
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's examples in the objective point of view section reference the chain_of_command concept (e.g., BAD[#chain_of_command] annotations), and child 3's examples also use it; the concept is established outside this span and seeded.

expected_cross_links.name: chain_of_command
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 1's examples in the fairness section may reference chain_of_command; child 3's examples also use it.

judgment_calls: Chose three children aligned with the major section boundaries: L1974-2124 (preset voice + fairness + real-world ties), L2125-2302 (seek truth / no agenda / objective pov), L2303-2400 (present perspectives + no topic off limits). Alternative was two children splitting at L2125, but the middle section is large enough to warrant its own child.
The chain_of_command concept is inherited and appears in examples across all children; it is seeded and expected to be linked by the parent, not provided by any child.
